title: Workload templating + deterministic golden-suite for kernel probing and prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current benchmark harness captures a narrow set of prefill/decode traces and uses ad-hoc seeds. This hides regression modes where kernel routing changes cause outlier latencies for uncommon but production-relevant workload shapes (e.g., long prefix + short decode, interleaved multi-turn chat). The CI gates are overly brittle to noise and occasionally flag benign variance or miss slow regressions that only appear under specific scheduling interactions.

Goal: Build a workload templating system and deterministic golden-suite that lets us generate families of controlled traces (prefix/continuation shapes, KV cache hits, attention sparsity patterns) and pair them with a hierarchical prefill/decode scheduler that can be stress-tested across kernel selection configurations. Add robust CI perf gates that use stable baselines, batch-aware comparisons, and outlier-resilient statistics.

Scope:
- Workload templating DSL that composes: model architecture params (seq len, kv-size), token distribution templates (dense vs sparse attention patterns), conversation templates (multi-turn with varying prefix reuse), and runtime knobs (batch sizes, device mapping).
- Deterministic golden-suite: seed families + canonical input templates to produce reproducible prefill/decodes across hardware/quant modes. Include metadata describing expected kernel routes for each seed to help detect unintended routing changes.
- CI perf gates: integrate golden-suite runs into presubmit for runtime-critical PRs and nightly regression tests. Gate metrics include p50/p95/p99 latency, decode throughput, and kernel-selection stability score. Use bootstrap confidence intervals and median-of-means to reduce false positives.
- Telemetry & diff tooling: enhance bench harness to emit per-kernel timing breakdowns, prefill vs decode traces, and a compact baseline diff that surfaces changed kernel counts and skew direction.

Out of scope for this ticket: full end-to-end autoscaling policy changes, dedicated capacity billing adjustments, and public docs for templates (follow-ups will cover docs and SDK exposure).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Workload templating DSL implemented and validated with at least 12 distinct template families (chat short/long, single-turn long-prefill, multi-turn reuse, high-attention-sparsity).
2) Deterministic golden-suite committed with stable seeds and a generation script. Golden runs reproducibly match stored baselines on two reference machines (A100-40GB, H100-80GB) within ±1% median latency.
3) CI perf gate manifest added: nightly golden-suite run + presubmit smoke with lightweight family subset. Gates must use median-of-means and not exceed 2% false-positive rate on historical data.
4) Bench harness emits per-kernel timing and kernel-selection attribution in JSON-lines artifacts stored to S3 (or internal artifact store) and linked in CI runs.
5) Migration doc and runbook created: steps for adding new templates, adding seeds, and investigating CI failures.
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting — aligned on DSL primitives and seed determinism requirements. Owners: Marco (impl), Priya (telemetry), Dave (CI integration).

2026-02-22: Prototype templating DSL v0.1 checked in. Supports seq_len, decode_len, prefix_reuse_rate, attention_mask_profiles. Added tests for deterministic RNG using per-seed PRNG with salted run-id.

2026-02-28: Discovered nondeterminism on H100 due to cuBLAS workspace allocation ordering; mitigation: pin allocator flags and record workspace hash in artifact metadata. Working with infra to make allocator flag default for bench lanes.
2026-03-03: First golden-suite run completed against A100 reference node. Baseline established and stored. Initial CI gate configuration drafted — using median-of-means across 5 subruns per template.

2026-03-05: Added kernel-selection attribution to bench harness artifacts. Instrumentation records candidate kernels considered and final kernel chosen per operator; useful for regression triage. Preparing PR for CI integration and dashboard wiring.
notes:
Implementation details: prefer a composable YAML-based template format that compiles to the bench runner's trace proto. Use deterministic PRNG (xoshiro128+) seeded with (template-id, seed-index, hardware-id). For CI gates, compute median-of-means across N=5 repeated runs; fall back to historical control charts for flagged runs to reduce operator noise.

Open questions: 1) How many template families are 'sufficient' for broad coverage? Proposal: start with 12, expand after initial 2-week telemetry review. 2) Thresholds for kernel-selection stability score — propose initial threshold 0.02 (2% of ops changed kernel) as actionable.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): templating DSL + generator, deterministic seeds, baseline run on A100. Phase 2 (1 sprint): per-kernel attribution + storage artifacts + dashboard wiring. Phase 3 (1 sprint): CI presubmit smoke + nightly gate + runbook and triage process. Rollout: start with internal runtime team canary, then enable nightly job for org.
risks: Nondeterminism due to hardware/driver differences; increased CI cost for nightly runs; potential for noisy gates initially leading to fatigue. Mitigations: pin allocator/driver flags in bench lanes, use subsampling in presubmit, tune gate thresholds after 2-week burn-in.
